title: Model & Route Economy Matrix — compact dashboard prototype and chart specs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Design a high-density, scannable Model & Route Economy Matrix for the Redwood Console that surfaces latency, throughput, token metrics, and per-1k-token cost in a single compact grid. Goal: enable platform and product engineers to compare model-route combinations quickly, spot regressions (latency tail, cost spikes), and initiate rollouts or fallbacks directly from the grid.

Why this ticket: current per-route dashboards are page-heavy and require clicking into multiple charts to correlate cost vs tail latency vs throughput. This matrix prototype consolidates signals into micro-widgets (sparklines, violin microcharts, badges) with row actions for rollouts, pinning, and variant compare.

Scope: Figma prototype + annotated chart spec for telemetry/engineering, review session with PM/ENG, and handoff assets (tokens, components, interaction flows). Does NOT include implementation work beyond a follow-up engineering ticket.

Key UX concepts: compact rows representing model-route pairs; columns: model badge, route name, latency p50/p95/p99 (numbers + mini-violin show distribution), throughput (rps) sparkline, tokens/request sparkline, cost-per-1k tokens (waterfall microchart showing token-cost breakdown: prompt vs completion vs embeddings), trend indicator (7d delta), health indicator (green/yellow/red based on SLO thresholds), and quick actions (pin, open rollout, compare variants). Hover card shows last 1h microtrace sample with link to full trace. Mobile breakpoint collapses tokens and cost into a single combined metric.

Design goals & metrics: reduce mean time-to-detect (MTTD) for regressions by 30% for power users; allow top-10 model-route triage in under 2 minutes; keep vertical density at <= 16 rows per viewport at 1080p.

Trade-offs and decisions considered:
- Density vs scannability: chose smaller font + glyphs but retained numeric p95 and p99 to support rapid decision-making.
- Client-side rendering cost: microcharts are rasterized server-side into SVG assets for list view to avoid console CPU spikes. Recommendation logged under engineering dependencies.
- Color usage: heatmap ramp for cost and a separate sequential palette for latency to avoid signal conflation; accessibility checks performed for color contrast and color-blind simulation.
- Live update frequency: default 60s in matrix; quick-refresh on hover for active rows.

Prototype interactions covered: pin/unpin row; open rollout modal (pre-fills model and route); compare overlay to show two model variants across same metrics; apply cost-sensitivity slider (shows predicted cost delta for X% traffic shift).

Deliverables:
- Figma prototype (list + detail hover) annotated for engineering
- Chart spec document (flat metrics list, sampling guidance, aggregation window)
- Handoff: component tokens, accessibility notes, and a short usability script for follow-up testing.

notes: Chart spec highlights (flat list): metrics: latency_ms_p50, latency_ms_p95, latency_ms_p99, throughput_rps, tokens_per_request_avg, tokens_per_request_p90, embeddings_cost_usd_per_1k, gen_cost_usd_per_1k, total_cost_usd_per_1k; aggregation windows: 1m/5m/1h/24h; downsampling: server-side 1s -> 1m rollup for list view; violin: use 50 buckets for distribution histograms; sparkline: smoothed moving average with 5-sample window. Color ramps: latency palette (sequential blue -> purple), cost heatmap (green->amber->red), health badges use semantic colors from design tokens.
